1 # YAML support for the Go language 2 3 [![PkgGoDev](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/goccy/go-yaml)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/goccy/go-yaml) 4 ![Go](https://github.com/goccy/go-yaml/workflows/Go/badge.svg) 5 [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/goccy/go-yaml/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/goccy/go-yaml) 6 [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/goccy/go-yaml)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/goccy/go-yaml) 7 8 9 10 # Why a new library? 11 12 As of this writing, there already exists a de facto standard library for YAML processing for Go: [https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml](https://github.com/go-yaml/yaml). However we feel that some features are lacking, namely: 13 14 - Pretty format for error notifications 15 - Direct manipulation of YAML abstract syntax tree 16 - Support for `Anchor` and `Alias` when marshaling 17 - Allow referencing elements declared in another file via anchors 18 19 # Features 20 21 - Pretty format for error notifications 22 - Supports `Scanner` or `Lexer` or `Parser` as public API 23 - Supports `Anchor` and `Alias` to Marshaler 24 - Allow referencing elements declared in another file via anchors 25 - Extract value or AST by YAMLPath ( YAMLPath is like a JSONPath ) 26 27 # Installation 28 29 ```sh 30 go get -u github.com/goccy/go-yaml 31 ``` 32 33 # Synopsis 34 35 ## 1. Simple Encode/Decode 36 37 Has an interface like `go-yaml/yaml` using `reflect` 38 39 ```go 40 var v struct { 41 A int 42 B string 43 } 44 v.A = 1 45 v.B = "hello" 46 bytes, err := yaml.Marshal(v) 47 if err != nil { 48 //... 49 } 50 fmt.Println(string(bytes)) // "a: 1\nb: hello\n" 51 ``` 52 53 ```go 54 yml := ` 55 %YAML 1.2 56 --- 57 a: 1 58 b: c 59 ` 60 var v struct { 61 A int 62 B string 63 } 64 if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(yml), &v); err != nil { 65 //... 66 } 67 ``` 68 69 To control marshal/unmarshal behavior, you can use the `yaml` tag. 70 71 ```go 72 yml := `--- 73 foo: 1 74 bar: c 75 ` 76 var v struct { 77 A int `yaml:"foo"` 78 B string `yaml:"bar"` 79 } 80 if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(yml), &v); err != nil { 81 //... 82 } 83 ``` 84 85 For convenience, we also accept the `json` tag. Note that not all options from 86 the `json` tag will have significance when parsing YAML documents. If both 87 tags exist, `yaml` tag will take precedence. 88 89 ```go 90 yml := `--- 91 foo: 1 92 bar: c 93 ` 94 var v struct { 95 A int `json:"foo"` 96 B string `json:"bar"` 97 } 98 if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(yml), &v); err != nil { 99 //... 100 } 101 ``` 102 103 For custom marshal/unmarshaling, implement either `Bytes` or `Interface` variant of marshaler/unmarshaler. The difference is that while `BytesMarshaler`/`BytesUnmarshaler` behaves like [`encoding/json`](https://pkg.go.dev/encoding/json) and `InterfaceMarshaler`/`InterfaceUnmarshaler` behaves like [`gopkg.in/yaml.v2`](https://pkg.go.dev/gopkg.in/yaml.v2). 104 105 Semantically both are the same, but they differ in performance. Because indentation matters in YAML, you cannot simply accept a valid YAML fragment from a Marshaler, and expect it to work when it is attached to the parent container's serialized form. Therefore when we receive use the `BytesMarshaler`, which returns `[]byte`, we must decode it once to figure out how to make it work in the given context. If you use the `InterfaceMarshaler`, we can skip the decoding. 106 107 If you are repeatedly marshaling complex objects, the latter is always better 108 performance wise. But if you are, for example, just providing a choice between 109 a config file format that is read only once, the former is probably easier to 110 code. 111 112 ## 2. Reference elements declared in another file 113 114 `testdata` directory contains `anchor.yml` file: 115 116 ```shell 117 ├── testdata 118    └── anchor.yml 119 ``` 120 121 And `anchor.yml` is defined as follows: 122 123 ```yaml 124 a: &a 125 b: 1 126 c: hello 127 ``` 128 129 Then, if `yaml.ReferenceDirs("testdata")` option is passed to `yaml.Decoder`, 130 `Decoder` tries to find the anchor definition from YAML files the under `testdata` directory. 131 132 ```go 133 buf := bytes.NewBufferString("a: *a\n") 134 dec := yaml.NewDecoder(buf, yaml.ReferenceDirs("testdata")) 135 var v struct { 136 A struct { 137 B int 138 C string 139 } 140 } 141 if err := dec.Decode(&v); err != nil { 142 //... 143 } 144 fmt.Printf("%+v\n", v) // {A:{B:1 C:hello}} 145 ``` 146 147 ## 3. Encode with `Anchor` and `Alias` 148 149 ### 3.1. Explicitly declared `Anchor` name and `Alias` name 150 151 If you want to use `anchor` or `alias`, you can define it as a struct tag. 152 153 ```go 154 type T struct { 155 A int 156 B string 157 } 158 var v struct { 159 C *T `yaml:"c,anchor=x"` 160 D *T `yaml:"d,alias=x"` 161 } 162 v.C = &T{A: 1, B: "hello"} 163 v.D = v.C 164 bytes, err := yaml.Marshal(v) 165 if err != nil { 166 panic(err) 167 } 168 fmt.Println(string(bytes)) 169 /* 170 c: &x 171 a: 1 172 b: hello 173 d: *x 174 */ 175 ``` 176 177 ### 3.2. Implicitly declared `Anchor` and `Alias` names 178 179 If you do not explicitly declare the anchor name, the default behavior is to 180 use the equivalent of `strings.ToLower($FieldName)` as the name of the anchor. 181 182 If you do not explicitly declare the alias name AND the value is a pointer 183 to another element, we look up the anchor name by finding out which anchor 184 field the value is assigned to by looking up its pointer address. 185 186 ```go 187 type T struct { 188 I int 189 S string 190 } 191 var v struct { 192 A *T `yaml:"a,anchor"` 193 B *T `yaml:"b,anchor"` 194 C *T `yaml:"c,alias"` 195 D *T `yaml:"d,alias"` 196 } 197 v.A = &T{I: 1, S: "hello"} 198 v.B = &T{I: 2, S: "world"} 199 v.C = v.A // C has same pointer address to A 200 v.D = v.B // D has same pointer address to B 201 bytes, err := yaml.Marshal(v) 202 if err != nil { 203 //... 204 } 205 fmt.Println(string(bytes)) 206 /* 207 a: &a 208 i: 1 209 s: hello 210 b: &b 211 i: 2 212 s: world 213 c: *a 214 d: *b 215 */ 216 ``` 217 218 ### 3.3 MergeKey and Alias 219 220 Merge key and alias ( `<<: *alias` ) can be used by embedding a structure with the `inline,alias` tag. 221 222 ```go 223 type Person struct { 224 *Person `yaml:",omitempty,inline,alias"` // embed Person type for default value 225 Name string `yaml:",omitempty"` 226 Age int `yaml:",omitempty"` 227 } 228 defaultPerson := &Person{ 229 Name: "John Smith", 230 Age: 20, 231 } 232 people := []*Person{ 233 { 234 Person: defaultPerson, // assign default value 235 Name: "Ken", // override Name property 236 Age: 10, // override Age property 237 }, 238 { 239 Person: defaultPerson, // assign default value only 240 }, 241 } 242 var doc struct { 243 Default *Person `yaml:"default,anchor"` 244 People []*Person `yaml:"people"` 245 } 246 doc.Default = defaultPerson 247 doc.People = people 248 bytes, err := yaml.Marshal(doc) 249 if err != nil { 250 //... 251 } 252 fmt.Println(string(bytes)) 253 /* 254 default: &default 255 name: John Smith 256 age: 20 257 people: 258 - <<: *default 259 name: Ken 260 age: 10 261 - <<: *default 262 */ 263 ``` 264 265 ## 4. Pretty Formatted Errors 266 267 Error values produced during parsing have two extra features over regular 268 error values. 269 270 First, by default, they contain extra information on the location of the error 271 from the source YAML document, to make it easier to find the error location. 272 273 Second, the error messages can optionally be colorized. 274 275 If you would like to control exactly how the output looks like, consider 276 using `yaml.FormatError`, which accepts two boolean values to 277 control turning these features on or off. 278 279 280 281 ## 5. Use YAMLPath 282 283 ```go 284 yml := ` 285 store: 286 book: 287 - author: john 288 price: 10 289 - author: ken 290 price: 12 291 bicycle: 292 color: red 293 price: 19.95 294 ` 295 path, err := yaml.PathString("$.store.book[*].author") 296 if err != nil { 297 //... 298 } 299 var authors []string 300 if err := path.Read(strings.NewReader(yml), &authors); err != nil { 301 //... 302 } 303 fmt.Println(authors) 304 // [john ken] 305 ``` 306 307 ### 5.1 Print customized error with YAML source code 308 309 ```go 310 package main 311 312 import ( 313 "fmt" 314 315 "github.com/goccy/go-yaml" 316 ) 317 318 func main() { 319 yml := ` 320 a: 1 321 b: "hello" 322 ` 323 var v struct { 324 A int 325 B string 326 } 327 if err := yaml.Unmarshal([]byte(yml), &v); err != nil { 328 panic(err) 329 } 330 if v.A != 2 { 331 // output error with YAML source 332 path, err := yaml.PathString("$.a") 333 if err != nil { 334 panic(err) 335 } 336 source, err := path.AnnotateSource([]byte(yml), true) 337 if err != nil { 338 panic(err) 339 } 340 fmt.Printf("a value expected 2 but actual %d:\n%s\n", v.A, string(source)) 341 } 342 } 343 ``` 344 345 output result is the following: 346 347 348 349 350 # Tools 351 352 ## ycat 353 354 print yaml file with color 355 356 357 358 ### Installation 359 360 ```sh 361 go install github.com/goccy/go-yaml/cmd/ycat@latest 362 ``` 363 364 # Looking for Sponsors 365 366 I'm looking for sponsors this library.
